emailSubject: FMB News | Government Generates ₱33.5 Million From Auction of Abandoned Goods | August 8, 2026 | 6:00 PM PHT
headline: How BOC Auctions Turn Forfeited Assets Into Public Funds
deck: The Bureau of Customs uses public auctions and negotiated sales to recover value from seized, abandoned and forfeited goods, with proceeds remitted to the national government.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Bureau of Customs continues to dispose of seized, abandoned and forfeited goods through public auctions and negotiated sales, converting idle assets into government revenue.

sections.heading: What we know
paragraphs: The BOC reported that auctions and negotiated sales generated ₱329.934 million from January to May 2026. The bureau said proceeds are recorded, accounted for and remitted to the national government.

The Department of Finance separately reported the July 29 turnover of more than ₱205 million from the negotiated sale of two forfeited Bugatti vehicles after earlier auctions failed to attract qualified bidders.

sections.heading: Background
paragraphs: The Customs Modernization and Tariff Act and Customs Administrative Order No. 03-2020 provide procedures for disposing of seized, abandoned and forfeited goods through public auction, negotiated sale, donation and other lawful modes.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The bulletin claimed a separate ₱33.48 million disposition on August 8, but its links did not resolve to an article or official report establishing that figure. FMB News has therefore excluded that unverified amount from this report.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Transparent disposal prevents forfeited assets from losing value and returns proceeds to public funds. Open notices, bidding records and remittance documentation are essential for public accountability.

sections.heading: What happens next
paragraphs: The BOC is expected to continue publishing notices for eligible forfeited goods and reporting the results of completed auctions and negotiated sales.
